A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoAct-1 and support comparison of the text, equations, tables, and figures. All 12 pages of v1 and 17 pages of v3 were readable, including v3 Appendices A-D; v1 ends with references.

before.justification: v1 reports original OSWorld experiments, backbone comparisons, efficiency analyses, and failure cases in Tables 1-3, Figure 3, and Section 4.6.

after.justification: v3 reports original OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena results, backbone and component ablations, efficiency analyses, and failure cases.

M1.justification: The three-agent architecture is retained, but the feedback procedure is ambiguous. v1 Section 3.2 and Figure 2 return a Programmer summary plus screenshot. v3 Figure 2 omits that screenshot and Table 6 explicitly says none is provided, while Section 3.3 still describes returning screenshots. This conflict prevents determining whether the procedure changed or its documentation was corrected inconsistently.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates only OSWorld. v3 adds WindowsAgentArena with 154 tasks, extending evaluation to Windows and applications such as Edge, Settings, File Explorer, and Windows utilities. This substantially broadens the tested operating environments and task coverage.

E2.justification: The OSWorld comparison adds OpenCUA and removes UI-TARS-72B-DPO, Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Claude 4 Sonnet, and Agent S2 with Gemini-2.5-Pro. The new WindowsAgentArena comparison includes Agent S, NAVI, and Agent S2. These are substantive changes to evaluated comparator membership, beyond updated citations or scores.

E3.justification: v3 adds Programmer-only and GUI-only control configurations for the component ablation in Table 4 and reports Windows evaluation at 15, 50, and 100 steps. The existing Programmer/GUI/Orchestrator limits remain 20/25/15, and rule-based success evaluation is retained. The OSWorld label changes from 100+ to 150 steps, with an early-termination explanation rather than evidence of a changed internal execution limit.

E4.justification: New Table 4 directly tests whether combining coding and GUI execution improves on either modality alone, addressing a central architectural question absent from v1. Appendix D retains the two original VSCode cases and adds reflection-error and hallucination analyses. The backbone comparison and Figure 3 efficiency analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, statistical significance tests, or comparable uncertainty estimates. Additional point estimates and changed scores in v3 do not change this reporting practice.

E6.justification: v3 adds Windows results reaching 52.5% and component-ablation results of 35.73% for coding only and 50.68% for GUI only. Table 3 revises the two alternative-backbone scores from 47.41% to 43.43% and from 53.12% to 58.72%. The reported 15-step Jedi score changes from 26.80% to 42.37%, exceeding CoAct-1's retained 39.81%. CoAct-1's headline OSWorld 60.76% and Figure 3's 10.15-step result remain unchanged.

T1.justification: New Section 3.1 mathematically defines observations, interaction history, a goal-conditioned policy, the union of GUI and coding action spaces, and hierarchical executor policies. v1 describes the system informally. This adds a limited formal problem definition, without new theorems, proofs, or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The core contribution remains an orchestrated hybrid of coding and GUI actions. v3 broadens the abstract, introduction, and conclusion's state-of-the-art claim to include 52.5% on WindowsAgentArena alongside the retained OSWorld result. The central architectural and efficiency claims otherwise remain.

C2.justification: v3 interprets the new ablation as evidence that coding offers efficiency but insufficient task coverage alone, while GUI execution supplies complementary capabilities. It revises the backbone discussion around role-specific model strengths and adds explanations of hidden intermediate errors and hallucinated planning in Appendix D. Appendix C also acknowledges that alternative open-source GUI operators were not tested.

D1.justification: v1 provides model families, AG2 implementation information, and round limits but no full prompts. v3 Appendix C supplies dated model identifiers, initialization guidance including a recommended 60-second VM wait, and complete agent and summarizer prompts in Tables 5-9. The front page adds a code-repository link. These substantially improve reproducibility documentation without establishing that all newly disclosed settings changed.

R1.justification: v3 adds references to OpenCUA, UI-TARS-2, Beyond Browsing, WindowsAgentArena, and prompt-formatting research, while removing the Anthropic system-card and DeepSeek-R1 references. It more explicitly distinguishes free-form coding from application-specific APIs or SDKs, but retains the overall positioning among GUI, modular, and hybrid agent systems.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the retained method exposition around formal policies and separate workflow/memory descriptions, reorganizes baseline descriptions into model categories, and rewrites the results discussion. The original main-text case study moves into an expanded Appendix D, alongside new disclosure and reproducibility appendices. The title and terminology are also revised.

P2.justification: v3 adopts the ICLR layout, redraws Figure 1, revises Figure 2 annotations, and updates Figure 3 labels and captions. The original overall and application-level OSWorld tables are reorganized into a grouped-domain table across step budgets. New Windows, component-ablation, and boxed prompt tables substantially change the document's visual organization.

improvement.justification: Table 4 addresses v1's important lack of direct component-level evidence for the hybrid design, while Windows evaluation broadens empirical support. Exact model identifiers and full prompts resolve substantial reproducibility omissions. Expanded failure analysis also improves understanding of limitations. These gains outweigh the unresolved screenshot-return inconsistency and unexplained revisions to existing scores; the improvement does not depend on a higher headline OSWorld result.
